findings.claim: The new parity test searches the whole flattened bin/lib/usage.sh instead of only the `findings` block. So a phrase that also appears elsewhere in the file does not catch drift. The pair "HEAD12-N.json" already appears at bin/lib/usage.sh:269, in the help of another verb. If someone removed or changed `HEAD12-N.json` in the findings help (bin/lib/usage.sh:388), the test would still pass. The test also does not pin the identifier wording `review is NAME/HEAD12-N` against the engine's `<feature>/<head12>-<n>`. Fix: cut the wrapper text down to the lines from `findings --feature` to the next verb (`stop-hook`) before the Contains checks, and add the identifier pair.
